City of Mati, Davao Oriental Dear Mr. Sungahid: This has reference to your letter dated 18 January 2018 requesting for this Department's legal opinion on "the validity oftheBaIibago Waterworks Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) and the authority of the City Government of Mati to enter the same despite the non-passage and disapproval of the said city's Water Investment Plan It must be emphasized that under Section 22 (a) (5) 1 and (c) of the Republic Act (RA) No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code Of 1991 " (LGC), local government units (LGUs) have the power to enter into contracts with other entities and these contracts can be in the form of a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA). Subject to the condition, under Section 22 (c) of the LGC, that such power to enter into a contract can be exercised by the LGU concerned through its local chief executive (LCE) provided that said official has been duly authorized by the sanggunian2 concerned. Consequently, under Section 458 of the LGC3, the sangguniang panlungsod has the power and authority to establish and proy_ide for the maintenance, repair and operation Of an Section 22. Corporate Powers. — (a) Every local government unit, as a corporation, shall have the following powers: (5) To enter into contracts; and xxx 2 (c) Unless otherwise provided in this Code, no contract may be entered into by the local chief executive in behalf of the local government unit without prior authorization by the sanggunian concerned. A legible copy of such contract shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the provincial capitol or the city, municipal or barangay hall. 3 Section 458. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. (a) The sangguniang panlungsod, as the legislative body of the city, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers orthe cit)üiS provided for under Section 22 of this Code, and shall:

efficient waterworks.bFurther,; under Section 17 (a) of the LGC4, an LGU may exercise other functions and) responsibilities .as are, necessary, appropriate, or incidental to effcient and effective provisions of the basic services and facilities for its residents. Accordingly, LGUs may enter into contracts to ensure active participation of the private sector within its territorial jurisdiction provided that it will "not prejudice the social attributes of basic services and facilities"5, i.e. such services and facilities are made available to the general public within a reasonable rate and able to meet the requirements of its populace. However, as a caveat, under the 1987 Philippine Constitution these contracts or other form of authorization for the operation of a public utility are "non-exclusive" in character6, thus, public participation is encouraged and may not be exclusively limited to a certain entity/service provider or group of entities, neither would an entity or group of entities be prioritized over equally qualified service provider/s. Based on the discussions above, the City Government of Mati is not precluded to enter into a MOA with another entity, in this case the Balibago Waterworks MOA, provided that it complied with the procedural requirements under the law. (5) Approve ordinances which shall ensure the efficient and effective delivery of the basic services and facilities as provided for under Section 17 of this Code, and in addition to said services and facilities, shall: (vii) Subject to existing laws, and provide for the maintenance, repair and operation of an efficient waterworks system to supply water for the inhabitants and to purify the source of the water supply, regulate the construction, maintenance, repair and use of hydrants, pumps, cisterns and reservoirs; protect the purity and quantity of the water supply of the city and, for this purpose, extend the coverage of appropriate ordinances over all territory within the drainage area of said water supply and within one hundred ( 100) meters of the reservoir, conduit, canal, aqueduct, pumping station, or watershed used in connection with the water service; and regulate the consumption, use or wastage of water and fix and collect charges therefor; 4 Section 17. Basic Services and Facilities. — (a) Local government units shall endeavor to be self-reliant and shall continue exercising the powers and discharging the duties and functions currently vested upon them. They shall also discharge the functions and responsibilities of national agencies and offices devolved to them pursuant to this Code. Local government units shall likewise exercise such other powers and discharge such other functions and responsibilities as are necessary, appropriate, or incidental to efficient and effective provisions of the basic services and facilities enumerated herein. s Article 30 of the LGC's Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) provides the following: ARTICLE 30. Commercialization and Privatization. — (b) Without prejudice to the social attributes of basic services and facilities, LGUs may tap the private sector in the delivery of basic services and facilities. 6 Section 11, Article XII of the 1987 Philippine Constitution.

It must also be considered that the MOA entered into by the concerned LGU is presumed valid until the contrary is proved in a proper proceeding. Since the aforementioned acts of the said LGU enjoy the presumption of regularity, this Department has no power to invalidate such acts. In addition, there was an allegation in the letter that the Water Investment Plan or Balibago Waterworks Investment of the concerned LGU was not approved by its respective Local Development Council (LDC). Although Section 109 (a) (2) Of the LGC provides that the LDC has the power to formulate the medium-term and annual public investment programs of the LGU concerned; however, it does not preclude the sanggunian concerned from identifying and/or introducing other plans, programs and projects which it may consider as to be given priority. Our Legal Opinion No. 230-93, s. 1993, provides the following: "...it could be understood from the foregoing provisions that the MDC (Municipal Development Council)? is the first step in the formulation of a comprehensive mufti-sectoral development plan, subject to the approval of the sangguniang bayan. This does not however, preclude the sarwunian from identifying and/or introducing other plans, programs and projects which it may consider as to be given priority, considering that under Section 114, hereinabove quoted the MDC's proposal shall have to be submitted to the SB for "appropriate action "; hence, it does not necessarily mean that the SB's approval is a ministerial functions as the said legislative body is likewise mandated to, among others, "generate and maximize the use of resources and revenues for the development plans, program objectives and priorities of the municipality" and shall "approve the annual and supplemental budgets of the municipal government and appropriate funds for specific programs, projects, services and activities of the municipality, or for other purposes not contrary to law, in order to promote the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants" (Section 447[2], RA 7160). " In connection therewith, assuming that there are other water associations located within the territorial jurisdiction of the concerned LGU, it does not give these water associations the right to be prioritized. Their capacity and capability of delivering waterworks services must be assessed by the said LGU subject to evaluation by relevant agencies and/or bodies. 7 | DC for a Municipality is called Municipal Development Council (MDC).

Lastly, as discussed above, because of the "non-exclusive" character of the contracts or other forms of authorization for the operation of a public utility, the same should "not be exclusively limited to a certain entity/service provider or group of entities, neither would an entity or group of entities be prioritized over equally qualified service provider/s". We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Aut of the Secretary: AUSETERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary 1018 2018-02-1 Legal/01 CV DIR. ALEX C.
